title: Meeting Robert Hoffman and the plan to learn organ
summary: Benny Mars introduces her to Hoffman, who was studying organ and offers to teach her what he learns.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh, I think it was when I was still playing at the Crest Doa. He had come back to New Orleans. He was a New Orleans man, alright, but he had been off somewhere else playing. And he came back into town and, um, uh, do you remember, do you know who Benny Mars was? A, a band leader that used to direct?
Yes, I know about him. Yeah, about him.

Well, he and my husband were friends. So, Benny Mars used to come into the store to get professional copies to the Crest store, yeah. And, uh, so one day he came in with this man and he introduced him to me. And, uh, so in talking, uh, Mr. Hoffman had started taking organ lessons from Bode Mala. Do you know who he was? He was, he was, uh, organist, uh, for the, uh, Jewish temple that's there on Carondelet Street where they, motion picture company.
I've seen his, I've seen his name. Uh-huh, Bode Mala.

Well, anyway, he was taking organ lessons from him. So, he said to me, if you will, he says, the coming thing in pictures is the organ. So, he says, if you'll get your organ to practice on, I'll teach you what Bode Mala teaches me. So, he got a book and gave it to me and I was, uh, going to the Christian church. That was my, really, home church, church I was, uh, raised in, up on St. Charles Avenue. And they said I could use the organ if they had a practice on. So, that's what I did. And pretty soon I got a job with, um, um, Fitchinburg, who was the first picture show people in town. I don't know that. Fitchinburg. And, um, when I look, I have a scrapbook. Oh. And I, I feel sure that I have, uh, in that scrapbook, I, I can show it to you. You can look at it as little or as much of it as you want to. Yeah. And it is, uh, a letterhead from Fitchinburg here. And, uh, they owned a place, uh, a picture show on the corner of Canal and Dortheen where Kassin Brestoff now sits. And Kassin Brestoff was next door. And this picture show was on the corner. And, um, so, uh, Mr. Hoffman, after I had, uh, of course, they, they didn't have an organ in that picture show. It was what was called an orgotron. It was a piano with two and a half octaves of organ that you played your right hand on. So, uh, he told me one day that, uh, the lady who played there had quit the night before. And why didn't I go down and ask for the job? So, I found out the man, that, in the meantime, I don't know whether Sanger had actually entered the field right at that moment or not. I don't remember that. But the manager had an office up over that picture show. And it's Mr. Geringer. Do you know that name?
